text: Overdosage 1. If marked excitement is present, a short acting barbiturate, chloral hydrate of paraldehyde may be used for sedation. Large doses should be avoided if possible and must be carefully controlled so that they will not add to the depressive stages of atropine poisoning. 2. Artificial respiration with oxygen is necessary when respiration is depressed. 3. Depression may be controlled by use of caffeine, sodium benzoate or picrotoxin together with the inhalation of oxygen. 4. As a physiologic antidote, neostigmine methylsulfate may be given by intramuscular injection in doses of 500 mcg to 1 mg and repeated every 2 to 9 hours. 5. Remaining therapy is purely symptomatic. Icebags and alcohol sponges help to reduce fever, especially in children. Careful nursing is essential. The room should be darkened, because of the patient’s marked photophobia.
